Q: GitHub shows "Processing updates" on my Pull Request after every push A:

It could be a temporary GitHub System Load issue as you mentioned, but in general, it could happen in these cases also:

  • GitHub System Load: As mentioned, at times of high demand or maintenance, GitHub may delay the processing of new commits and PR updates. These temporary system bottlenecks can cause your commits to be "queued" for display.

  • CI Delays: If your repository is linked to Continuous Integration tools like GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or others, the new commit will sometimes wait for the CI pipeline to initialise before fully updating the PR. Even if the commit has been pushed, GitHub might delay showing it to ensure that all checks are run without issues.

  • Branch Protection Rules: If you have branch protection rules in place (such as requiring status checks to pass before commits appear), it could sometimes slow down the update process.

  • Force Pushing: If you're force-pushing changes to the PR branch, GitHub may take more time to process the new commit history.

Q: Exporting SQL Table into a CSV file using Windows Batch Script A:

Use the sqlcmd utility.

You need to modify the code to make it work in your environment, but here goes.

if not exist "%MYHOME%\net\" mkdir "%MYHOME%\net"
"C:\your path\to\sqlcmd.exe" -S YourDBServer -d DB_NAME -E -Q "select id, a_id, alias, address, domain, mask from net_network" -o "CSV-EXPORT-FILE.csv" -s "," -w 255

Some explanations:

-S The database server to connect to.
-d Name of the database to connect to.
-Q Query to run, can also be insert, delete, update etc.
-o select the output file
-s "," separated by comma
-w column width, this must be as big as your largest columns characters.

Q: Type of the Variable to Store a Type Information of Another Variable A:

The type of a variable that stores type information (int, str etc.) is called a type Object.

Example:

x = int
print(type(x))

It will output:

<class 'type'>

Simply:

  • Variable that stores value can be int, str etc.

  • Variable that stores a type is always type.
